messages.subject: Exorbitant Memory Use with ddply
parts:
When I use ddply on a data frame with approximately 25k rows, it keeps using memory until it gets to 80% of available memory and then it seems like my Linux system throttles CPU usage to less than 2%.  I'm trying to prepare a data frame for casting from long to wide per this instruction. 

The data frame:

> head(yat3)
  sch_no grade subject mean
1   6730     3    Math   NA
2   6730     3 Reading   NA
3   6730     4    Math   NA
4   6730     4 Reading   NA
5   6730     4 Writing   NA
6   6730     5    Math   NA
 
> nrow(yat3)
[1] 25592

The command:

tmp <- ddply(yat3, .(sch_no, grade), transform, newid = paste(sch_no, grade))

If I issue the following command it finishes promptly:

yat3$newid <- paste(yat3$sch_no, yat3$grade)

Am I doing something wrong?   Or is this a bug?

Thanks!

Think about what this is doing. Assuming theat Math and Reading are
the only subjects, you are splitting your file into 25000/2 pieces and
running the paste function on each one. Thats going to take some time
and resources, and it's entirely unclear why you want to do this.

>
>
> If I issue the following command it finishes promptly:
>
> yat3$newid <- paste(yat3$sch_no, yat3$grade)

Do that. As far as I can see the restult should be identical to what
the ddply code above would eventually give you.

>
>
> Am I doing something wrong? Or is this a bug?

Just that you're making life more difficult for yourself than it neeeds to be...
